long_description: Veesion is an AI-powered retail security company founded in 2018 by Benoît Koenig, Damien Ménigaux, and Thibault David. Headquartered in Paris, France, with an office in Bordeaux, Veesion employs around 150 people. The company focuses on software development in the fields of artificial intelligence and retail security, aiming to make AI accessible to professionals worldwide. Veesion's main product is its AI-powered video analytics platform, which integrates seamlessly with existing CCTV systems. The software features real-time gesture recognition to detect suspicious behaviors, such as bag concealment and item hoarding, while prioritizing privacy by avoiding facial recognition. It provides instant alerts to store staff and is compatible with both analog and digital cameras. Veesion operates in over 25 countries, providing security solutions for more than 5,000 stores globally, including supermarkets and pharmacies. The company is recognized for its innovative approach to theft prevention and enhancing overall store security.

long_description: Tricog Health is a global health technology company founded in 2014, headquartered in Bengaluru, India, with a legal entity in Singapore. The company specializes in AI-powered virtual cardiac diagnostic tools and services, aiming to provide healthcare providers with accurate and timely diagnoses of heart conditions. Tricog operates in 14 to 16 countries across India, Southeast Asia, and Africa, having screened over 10 million patients and saved more than 400,000 lives. Tricog's mission is to enable accessible and affordable cardiac care for all. The company offers a comprehensive cardiology platform that includes products like InstaECG, an AI-driven electrocardiogram diagnostic solution, and InstaEcho, an AI-powered echocardiogram tool. These tools facilitate real-time detection and management of cardiac conditions, addressing gaps in cardiac care infrastructure. Tricog primarily serves healthcare providers, physicians, and medical device manufacturers, focusing on expanding cardiac diagnostic capabilities in areas with limited access to specialized cardiologists.
